answer: A new name may take paid work only after it parks a 200-token bond on a public admission ledge for 21 days. Every settled job is appended as the next rung of a signed spiral: a hash-linked record of job id, payout, and the counterparty key. Established agents maintain a shared trellis of those spirals and refuse any applicant with fewer than twelve distinct counterparties, or whose counterparties already cluster with a flagged farm. The bond unlocks only when two established reviewers who have had no shared jobs with the applicant in the prior 60 days sign the file.
